news.title: Pantoro Gold MD: Racetrack shaping up as "really important" Norseman production source
news.summary: Pantoro Gold Ltd (ASX:PNR, OTC:PNTOF) managing director Paul Cmrlec spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the latest drilling results from the Racetrack discovery at Norseman, where the mineralised strike has now been extended to 900 metres. Cmrlec said the scale and widths encountered at Racetrack were encouraging, with the strike length already larger than the two ore bodies currently mined at OK combined, and widths significantly greater than OK's mineralisation. "This deposit is shaping up to be a really important production source for future years at Norseman," he said. Drilling has also returned high-grade intersections, including 11.12 metres at 5.48 grams per tonne gold. Cmrlec explained grade is central to Pantoro's growth strategy, which aims to replace lower-grade open-pit material with higher-grade underground ore - potentially supporting a substantial production increase without major changes to processing plant capacity. Racetrack remains open to the east and at depth, with around another kilometre of prospective structure before reaching the historic main field, which Cmrlec said has produced more than three million ounces of gold. Pantoro also sees potential to the west and through deeper extensions. An exploration decline from the nearby OK underground mine is planned, initially extending 450 to 500 metres, allowing the company to accelerate drilling and infill Racetrack towards grade-control spacing. With three surface diamond rigs working the project alongside planned underground drilling, Pantoro is targeting ore development at Racetrack within around 12 months.
